metadata.title: OPT Countdown: Final Project Pitch
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: A pitch, not a lesson: no verdict card and no Your Turn. The outro is my own drawn card, because the stock ClaudeTitleOutro hardcodes the instructor's handle and this assignment forbids using it.
metadata.audience: INFO 7375 reviewers; hiring managers for new-grad SWE / data analyst roles
metadata.source_doc: PROJECT-BRIEF.md; the opt-countdown prototype (PR nikbearbrown/the-reallocation-engine#48, commit 81d0161), re-run 2026-10-13

skin_warnings: BIDEA: palette=claude but the cold open is 'BrutalistHesitantWriter' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk
BOUT: palette=claude but the outro is 'un-annotated' — OUTRO LAW wants ClaudeTitleOutro

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Saloni, and this is the pitch for my final project. Part of it exists today as a prototype. Most of it doesn't yet, and I'll say which is which. A student on O P T asks, which jobs can I get? The better question is, which jobs can I start in time?

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer opener: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Here's the one sentence. O P T Countdown will be a command-line tool, in a public GitHub repository. You give it your O P T dates and a list of job postings. For each posting, it says apply, network first, skip, or blocked, and it shows the evidence behind every answer.

shot.visual_intent: Constructed sketch: posting pages slide into a kraft box (the tool) and land in four labelled stacks.
shot.motion_claim: Constructed sketch: posting pages slide into a kraft box (the tool) and land in four labelled stacks.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: First, what exists today. For the Reallocation Engine assignment, I built a prototype of this. On October thirteenth I ran it again. Twelve of twelve tests passed. It sorted eight postings for a fictional student with fifty-three days left: one apply, two network first, three skip, and two blocked. Everything after this is what I will build.

shot.visual_intent: Real output, dated: a counter climbs to 12/12 tests; four grey bars grow to 1, 2, 3, 2.
shot.motion_claim: Real output, dated: a counter climbs to 12/12 tests; four grey bars grow to 1, 2, 3, 2.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Why would anyone care? Today a student checks each posting by hand. Look up the employer's H one B record, which is its history of sponsoring work visas. Open the posting to see if it's still live. Guess how fast they hire. Count the days. I guessed about twenty minutes a posting. That's an estimate. I haven't timed it.

shot.visual_intent: One posting page; four step marks appear around it while a clock hand sweeps; '20 min, estimate'.
shot.motion_claim: One posting page; four step marks appear around it while a clock hand sweeps; '20 min, estimate'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The engine I built on already has a liveness checker. I gave it a fake job link. It said active, because the dead link redirects to a live careers page. Greenhouse's own job API said four oh four, not found. In my tool, the API answer wins.

shot.visual_intent: A page with 'checker: active'; a scan line sweeps; a server stack answers '404'; the check is struck out.
shot.motion_claim: A page with 'checker: active'; a scan line sweeps; a server stack answers '404'; the check is struck out.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The raw H one B data has a similar trap. HubSpot has no row at all, and DraftKings has blank fields. A naive tool reads that silence as, won't sponsor, and skips them. Mine marks them blocked, for a person to check.

shot.visual_intent: A data table; two rows stay empty; their pages slide to a 'blocked' stack instead of the bin.
shot.motion_claim: A data table; two rows stay empty; their pages slide to a 'blocked' stack instead of the bin.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: And neither one checks the clock. O P T allows ninety days of unemployment. A strong sponsor that takes sixty days to hire is no use to someone with fifty-three days left. In the prototype run, Klaviyo and Toast were skipped for exactly that reason.

shot.visual_intent: Two bars: runway 53 days, hiring time 60 days; the second overshoots the first's end.
shot.motion_claim: Two bars: runway 53 days, hiring time 60 days; the second overshoots the first's end.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A student on O P T runs one command and reads a one-page report. And a hiring manager or engineer, for the new-grad software and data analyst roles I'm aiming at, opens the read me, runs the tests, and looks at the evaluation log, all in the first minute.

shot.visual_intent: Constructed sketch: a repository window; a cursor clicks; three rows get checks: README, tests, eval log.
shot.motion_claim: Constructed sketch: a repository window; a cursor clicks; three rows get checks: README, tests, eval log.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: What would it prove about me? Verification: every number carries a label saying where it came from. Evaluation: I'll hand-label postings and measure how often each check is wrong. Source grounding: no record, no answer. It would not prove the tool gets anyone hired, and I won't claim that.

shot.visual_intent: Constructed sketch: a report page; three source tags snap onto its rows: record, your input, model guess.
shot.motion_claim: Constructed sketch: a report page; three source tags snap onto its rows: record, your input, model guess.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: What's out? Immigration advice. Rules like cap-gap and the STEM extension stay with the school's D S O. What comes first? Move the prototype into its own repository, so a stranger can clone it, run the tests, and watch them pass in a fresh copy.

shot.visual_intent: A page marked 'immigration advice' slides toward the box and is pushed back; then a fresh box gets a check.
shot.motion_claim: A page marked 'immigration advice' slides toward the box and is pushed back; then a fresh box gets a check.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: What could sink it? The hiring times are my own guesses, and they decide many answers. The only apply in my run cleared the bar by just point zero one seven. So the report will show which answers would flip if a guess moved fifteen days either way.

shot.visual_intent: A scale with the 0.30 bar; a dot lands at 0.317, just above it; a question mark appears beside it.
shot.motion_claim: A scale with the 0.30 bar; a dot lands at 0.317, just above it; a question mark appears beside it.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture on a cream stage per beat, with the voice carrying the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix, but more learning than showing off. I already know JavaScript and Node. My evidence is CodeBuddies, my Node team project from an earlier course. What's new to me is building a labelled evaluation set and measuring a tool's own error rate. And to be honest, Claude Code did most of the typing on the prototype while I directed it. How many postings the evaluation needs, I don't know yet. I'll start with thirty, and watch how much the error rate moves.

shot.visual_intent: Two boxes: a taped box 'have: Node' gets a check; an open box 'learning: evals' fills with pages.
shot.motion_claim: Two boxes: a taped box 'have: Node' gets a check; an open box 'learning: evals' fills with pages.
